The buttons swap sides, and the locale sets the digits and the currency.

The field follows the keyboard of the WAI-ARIA spinbutton pattern on a native text input, so ordinary text editing keeps working. Name the input with a label or `aria-label`. The step buttons are named “Increase” and “Decrease” by default, point at the input, and stay out of the tab order because the arrow keys do the same.

The value is a number, or `null` when the field is empty, while the field shows it formatted. Typing updates the value once the text is a valid number. Enter or leaving the field commits it: the text is read, kept within `min` and `max`, snapped to the step and formatted again.
The variant: split, stacked or plain.
Turns off this button alone.
With `wheel`, scrolling over the focused field steps the value. It’s off by default, so a page that scrolls past the field never changes it.
With a `name`, the number submits as is, like 1250, never formatted. `required` blocks an empty field, and a form reset returns to the default.
With an arrow key, steps by smallStep, a tenth of a step by default.
`format` takes `Intl.NumberFormat` options. People can type in the same format, and a percent is a fraction, so 15% is 0.15. The `variant="stacked"` group puts small chevrons at the end.
`invalid` marks the field and sets `aria-invalid` on the input, for checks of your own like stock.
`locale` picks separators, symbols and digit grouping, for showing and for typing. Without it, the field follows the page’s language once it’s interactive, and the server renders English.
`onValueChange` runs on every valid change, and `onValueCommit` once an interaction ends, which is the one to save on. A controller steps or sets the value from any button.
`step` is the usual increment. Shift, Page Up and Page Down move by `largeStep`, and Alt or Option with an arrow key by `smallStep`. Hold a button to repeat.
